clue.text: One after the other giving support to footballer

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
taken as written
a back is a defensive player in football

explanation.surface: A fan cheering on a favourite player from the stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Things happening consecutively, in unbroken succession, come in a row like that.

clue.text: Buying opportunity provided by high street chain with beer

parts.note: Boots is a chain of chemist's shops found on British high streets
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A shopping trip to a chemist's followed by a pint at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOTS is a British chain of pharmacies; a BOOT SALE is a sale of second-hand goods from car boots.
explanation.definitionFit: A car-boot sale is an outdoor market where bargains can be bought from the backs of cars.

clue.text: Heraldic device seen under church entrances

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is placed beneath the first, so it sits under it

parts.note: a coat of arms is the heraldic device of a family

explanation.surface: A coat of arms carved below the doorways of a parish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrances' looks like doorways, but it is the verb: to entrance is to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to delight or bewitch them, the verb sense of enchanting.

clue.text: The nights a woman goes out in clingy attire

indicators.note: the woman's letters leave the phrase, going out of it

parts.note: hen is an informal word for a woman

explanation.surface: Evenings when a woman goes out dressed in figure-hugging clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing HEN from THE NIGHTS leaves T + IGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery that fits closely over the legs and hips is close-fitting clothing.

clue.text: Robert may turn to a branch of meteorology

indicators.note: the letters of the name turn into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Robert might change career and take up weather science.
explanation.definitionFit: The measurement of atmospheric pressure is one specialist field within weather science.

clue.text: Man embracing girl with energy that may be burning

indicators.note: one name holds the other within its arms, so it goes around it

parts.note: Ken is a man's name
Rose is a girl's name
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A passionate couple hugging with a burning energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin oil is a fuel used in lamps and heaters, so it is often alight.

clue.text: Island to get spiced up and warm

definitions.meaning: an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

definitions.text: to get spiced up and warm
definitions.meaning: the verb used of wine heated with spices

explanation.surface: Island
explanation.definitionFit: One is a Hebridean isle; the other is the verb for heating wine with spices, as at Christmas.

clue.text: Studied intensively, being set upon at university

parts.note: to be mugged is to be attacked and robbed
up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student assaulted while away at college.
explanation.walkthrough: To be UP is British usage for being at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To swot hard for an exam is British slang for cramming a subject.

clue.text: A letter I redrafted, making it scholarly

indicators.note: a redrafted text has its words or letters reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone rewriting their correspondence to sound more learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-read and educated is the broader sense of able to read and write.

clue.text: Old variety of products, lines coming from fruit plantation

parts.note: a range is the full line of goods a firm offers
RY, short for railway, is a set of lines

explanation.surface: An old assortment of goods and railway lines leading out of an orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: RY (railway) for 'lines' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A glasshouse for growing citrus trees is a place where such fruit is cultivated.

clue.text: Entitlements of the two joined in marriage, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is only spoken like the one we need

parts.note: the ceremonies by which a couple are wed are rites

explanation.surface: A question of what a married couple are each entitled to.
explanation.walkthrough: The ceremony, or rites, of marriage joins the couple; the word spoken is the same as the one for entitlements.
explanation.definitionFit: Things one is legally or morally owed are one's due claims.

clue.text: One day with awful mites around 'ouse?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the other piece
awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess and must be rearranged

parts.note: a Cockney dropping the h of house or home; here the h-less home

explanation.surface: A Cockney complaining about a plague of mites around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' makes an anagram and 'around' a container; the apostrophe in 'ouse marks a Cockney dropped H, so read it as the h-less word for home.
explanation.definitionFit: At some unspecified future point is what an indefinite day means.

clue.text: Bashful about sin engendered by drink

indicators.note: one word is wrapped about the other

parts.note: bashful means shy
to err is to sin or go wrong

explanation.surface: A shy person committing a sin after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from Spain is a common alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: To boot a number outside hospital

indicators.note: the number sits outside the letter for hospital, around it

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Kicking a number of people out of the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To boot' looks like kicking; it means moreover, in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as moreover or besides, the word adds a further point, as in addition.

clue.text: Thus one may be very grateful for good

definitions.text: Thus one may be very grateful
definitions.meaning: the phrase used of lasting gratitude, as in being grateful forever

explanation.surface: Someone thankful for a kindness done to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting forever describes both an undying gratitude and something permanent.

clue.text: English copper met with endless love in the country

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the word for love loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: to adore is to love

explanation.surface: An English policeman finding romance abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but here it is the metal, symbol CU; ADORE loses its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American nation on the equator is the state named here.

clue.text: About to go on an area having crossed a waterfall

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece goes on top of the next, so it comes first

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: the stretch of land crosses over the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A hiker about to set off across country to see a cascade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' as circa is a convention; 'to go on' places it first in this down entry, and 'having crossed' wraps the land around the lone letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large steep waterfall or cascade is the original sense, later used of the eye condition.

clue.text: As members may be linked up

definitions.text: As members may be linked up

parts.words: As members may be linked up
parts.note: members here are limbs; two people walking with limbs looped together

explanation.surface: Club members joining together for a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' suggests club members, but it means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking with linked elbows is how a close pair stroll together.

clue.text: Old theologian — one joins nonconformists

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theology degree, so a theologian
I is the Roman numeral for one
to tie is to join

explanation.surface: An elderly churchman joining a dissenting chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonconformists' suggests Methodists or Baptists, but it simply means eccentric people.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric characters who do not fit in are odd people or things.

clue.text: The heartless politician beginning to taunt the queen — persuasive type?

indicators.note: the word loses its central letter, its heart

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted politician starting to mock the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lures or entices others into doing wrong is a seducer.

clue.text: Get back on journey, leaving quietly on 24 December?

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: the letter for quietly leaves the word for a journey

parts.note: a trip is a journey
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
the 24th of December is Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: Someone collecting a gift by travelling quietly on Christmas Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover or fetch something is to bring it back again.

clue.text: Some rowdy neighbours? Get the force

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Noisy people next door prompt a call to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the force' reads as calling the police; 'Get the' is a link and only 'force' defines, the draft's 'Get the force' does not swap for a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small unit of force in the centimetre-gram-second system is named here.

clue.text: Son to run off in fast race

parts.note: to run off copies is to print them

explanation.surface: A boy running off in a quick race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run off' suggests fleeing, but it means producing copies on a press.
explanation.definitionFit: A short race at full speed is a dash.

clue.text: Among the stars a domineering woman

indicators.note: the letter goes among, so inside, the constellation's name

parts.note: Virgo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A bossy woman who thinks she belongs among the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce or bullying woman is a shrew or harridan.

clue.text: Island volunteers greeting the immigrants initially

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
hi is a greeting

indicators.note: the first letters of the next words are taken

explanation.surface: Volunteers on an island welcome newly arrived migrants.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pacific island in French Polynesia is the place named.

clue.text: One tucking into fish becomes more irritable

indicators.note: the letter is tucked inside the fish's name

parts.note: a snapper is a kind of fish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone eating a fish dinner and getting grumpier.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sharper-tempered and quicker to bite back is a comparative of curt.

clue.text: Sarah and French friend providing food

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: Sarah and her French pal bringing a picnic.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiced cured sausage is an item to eat.

clue.text: Given pen this one would have come a place higher!

definitions.text: Given pen this one would have come a place higher!

parts.words: Given pen this one would have come a place higher
parts.note: adding the letters pen in front turns the word for last into the word for second to last

explanation.surface: A competitor who would have finished one place better with a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: Prefix PEN- and the word becomes 'penultimate', last but one, a place higher than last.
explanation.definitionFit: Final or last in a series is the plain meaning; the clue plays on its longer relative.

clue.text: A cat? It isn't very big

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A small kitten prompts the question whether it is a cat at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of a chemical element is tiny indeed.

clue.text: Mate has toy to play with — someone stuck indoors

indicators.note: the letters are toys to play with and rearrange

explanation.surface: A friend has a toy to keep a housebound person amused.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rarely goes out is a homebody or recluse.
